mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investments, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the periods with declining RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (proxied by INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (proxied by PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure under tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a weakening demand and labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (proxied by GDPC1) over three consecutive quarters signals a strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the periods with increasing GDPC1.
